title: Click ingestion handler with budget ledger
name: Click budget ingestion

questions.prompt: Is there a defect in how this code handles bad input at the HTTP boundary? If so, mark the line(s) where it is; otherwise answer that there is none.
Why does BudgetLedger lock with `.unwrap_or_else(PoisonError::into_inner)` instead of `.unwrap()`?
choices: Because lock() cannot fail, so the call is only there to satisfy the compiler
So a panic in some other thread that held the mutex does not make every later charge or refund panic
So the lock is released automatically when the request times out
So multiple threads can hold the lock at once for read-only access

questions.prompt: The INSERT fails because the database is unreachable. What does the client observe, and what happens to the campaign budget?
choices: A 500 from the panic handler; the budget stays reduced
A 503 with a generic message; the charge is refunded so the budget is unchanged
A 503 with the sqlx error text in the body; the budget stays reduced
A 202, because the error is only logged

questions.prompt: Where does the layer ordering `.layer(TimeoutLayer ...).layer(CatchPanicLayer ...)` place panic handling relative to the timeout?
choices: CatchPanicLayer is added last, so it wraps the timeout and the handler; a panic anywhere inside becomes the 500 response
TimeoutLayer wraps CatchPanicLayer, so a timeout is converted into a panic
The order does not matter in axum; both layers run on every request in parallel
CatchPanicLayer only applies to routes registered after it was added
